Greater Production Scheme - Interest on other Trust Accounts Transposed to Greater Production Account

AUDIT OFFICE, December 21, 1923.

SIR, - In examining the statements rendered by Mr. W.M. Graham in connection with the Greater Production Scheme,
I find that he has credited the Greater Production Account with the interest allowed by the bank on the amounts on
deposit in two other of his Trust Accounts, viz: Grazing Leases Account and Indian Bands Trust Account. The first of
these accounts consists of the amounts collected for the lease of Indian lands, which amounts are ultimately distributed
among the Indians or transmitted to the department to be placed to the credit of the bands concerned. The second
account consists chiefly of amounts received from your department for distribution to the Indians.

When Mr. Reid of this office visited the Regina office last summer he was given to understand by Mr. Graham that the
reason that the interest accruing



=== EXTRACT FROM HERE (pages 614-617) ===
<!-- page 614 -->
on these accounts was transferred to the credit of the Greater Production Account was that as the interest could not be
said to belong to any particular band or bands it could not be distributed, and it was accordingly considered that it
might be transferred to the Greater Production Account.

I am of opinion that the interest in these two accounts should not have been so transferred to the Greater Production
Account with which it had no direct connection, but that, as it could not be assigned to any particular band of Indians
it should have been remitted to your department as Casual Revenue.

The total interest thus transferred from the time of the inception of the Greater Production account up to March 31st
last was $902.90, made up as follows: -

...       Grazing Leases Account Indian Bands Trust Account
1919 - 20 $35 91                 ...
1920 - 21 289 43                 $262 62
1921 - 22 125 14                 117 26
1922 - 23 46 11                  76 43
...       $446 59                $456 31

I think that Mr. Graham should be now requested to take this amount from his Greater Production account and to remit
it to your department as Casual Revenue.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

Surplus Military Stores - Regina Warehouse Account

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, December 4, 1922.

SIR, - On inquiry of your Accountant with respect to certain transfers made by Mr. W.M. Graham from Regina
"Warehouse Account" to "Greater Production Account" I was informed by him that "when large quantities of clothing,
equipment, hospital supplies, etc., were taken over from the Militia and Defence and from the Soldiers" Civil Re-
Establishment Departments, they were stored in our Regina warehouse and are being sold to Indians and schools, and
all expenses including wages, etc., are being defrayed from the proceeds of the sales."

I beg to say that this procedure is not in accordance with the Consolidated Revenue and Audit Act. Although these
stores may have been transferred by the other departments to your department free of charge they still remain
government stores and the disposal of them must be accounted for in the same way as surplus stores acquired by your
department by purchase would be accounted for. The creation of a special fund administered by Mr. Graham or by any
other officer of your department is not in my opinion authorized by Statute or by any regulations of the Treasury made
thereunder. The actual proceeds of all sales must be deposited to the credit of the Receiver General, and any
expenditure incurred in connection with the care or the disposal of the stores must be made in the ordinary way
through your appropriation.

<!-- page 615 -->
Kindly furnish me with a statement showing in detail the supplies taken over by your department with any valuation
that may have been put on the same; also the particulars in detail of all sales and all expenditures to date, supported
with proper vouchers. All moneys at present in Mr. Graham's hands in connection with the "Warehouse Account"
should be deposited at once by him to the credit of the Receiver General.

I am, Sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, OTTAWA, December 28, 1922.

SIR, - In reply to your letter of the 4th instant respecting the disposal at Regina of supplies transferred to this
department by the Department of Militia and Defence and the Soldiers' Civil Re-Establishment Department, I have to
say that when the department was offered these large quantities of supplies, it was faced with the problem of storing
and distributing them to the best advantage possible. It was decided that Regina was the most central point and
facilities had to be provided for, viz: a warehouse, staff, and other incidental expenses. There was no appropriation by
Parliament to meet this expenditure and one could not be obtained without increasing our estimates, which was not
permissible. As schools drawing grants and Indians who had funds could be served from these stores at less cost than
if they had to purchase elsewhere, sales have been made to them, and a fund thus established to meet all expenses of
building a warehouse, paying wages, transportation charges and all other incidental expenses. Monthly statements of
all receipts and expenditure by Mr. Graham, together with vouchers, have been rendered, and these will be submitted
to you forthwith for examination.

Mr. Graham has also been requested to furnish a statement showing in detail the supplies taken over with any
valuation that may have been put on them.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
DUNCAN C. SCOTT, Deputy Supt. General.

The Auditor General of Ottawa.

NOTE. - Statements of the receipts and payments to June 30th, 1923, by Mr. Graham in connection with these surplus
supplies will be found on page I - 101 of this Report.

Surplus Military Supplies shipped to various Indian Superintendencies and Agencies

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, December 21, 1923.

SIR, - From statements rendered me by the Departments of Soldiers' Civil Re-establishment and of Militia and
Defence of the surplus stores transferred to your department, I learn that, besides the stores shipped to Mr. Graham at
Regina, a considerable quantity were transferred to your department at Ottawa and that shipments were also made to
various superintendencies and agencies throughout the Dominion.

<!-- page 616 -->
I am already in receipt of statements with regard to the stores shipped to Regina, but so far have received no
statements regarding the shipments to other points. Kindly let me know how these stores were dealt with at the various
superintendencies and agencies as well as in your department. Were any of these stores sold, or were they all
distributed gratuitously to the Indians? I should like to be furnished with any returns and statements that may have
been received in your department in connection with these stores.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

Public Moneys from whatever Source of Revenue Derived should be Paid to Credit of Receiver General

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, February 23, 1923.

SIR, - I have received from your Accountant's Office statements, with vouchers, up to December 31st last, of Mr.
W.M. Graham's Elkhorn School Account.

This account, which appears to be of the nature of a trust account and which dates back to July, 1918, may be
summarized as follows: -

Balance received from Rev. A. Wilson, principal                   $191 80
Proceeds of sales of grain, hay and potatoes                      4,243 66
Proceeds of sale of cattle                                        487 00
Rental of buildings and pasture                                   147 50
Compensation for tent burned                                      35 00
Interest allowed by bank                                          295 08
...                                                            $5,400 04
Less expenses in connection with gathering and marketing crops 1,331 62
Balance, December 31st, 1922                                   $4,068 42

I have been given to understand by your accountant that it is the intention of your department to reopen this school in
the coming spring and that the balance of this account will be applied to the re-establishment of the school. It appears
to me that this manner of dealing with the earnings of the school is a wrong one, and contrary to the provisions of the
Consolidated Revenue and Audit Act, which requires in Section 35, that all public moneys, from whatever source of
revenue derived, shall be paid to the credit of the Receiver General. Since the whole expenses in connection with the
maintenance of this school are paid from public funds, I am of opinion that any earnings of the school must be
regarded as public moneys, and as such should be dealt with in accordance with Section 35 of the Audit Act referred to
above.

I should also like to have some information with regard to the amount of $191.80 handed to Mr. Graham by Rev. A.E.
Wilson. Was this the balance of a trust account administered by Mr. Wilson, and if so, what was the nature of that
account?

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

<!-- page 617 -->
DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN'S AFFAIRS, OTTAWA, March 9, 1923.

DEAR MR. KEARNS, - I have to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of the 27th February, 1923.

When these funds came into the hands of the department from the Indian Commissioner, the intention was to use them
for the purchase of necessary equipment for the Elkhorn Industrial School which is to be opened under the auspices of
the Church of England, and by doing so the appropriation for Indian education would be supplemented. This method
of dealing with the small fund would be preferable to a refund to Casual Revenue. Any purchases charged to this
credit would, of course, be made under the control of the Purchasing Commission and would be subject to your audit.

I would point out that these amounts accrued from the sales at the closing of the school; the item of $191.80 as shown
in the bank book kept by Mr. A.E. Wilson - trust account - may have arisen from the sale of produce. The bank book
is open to your inspection.

If you find any unsurmountable difficulty in the way of letting us use the funds, kindly let me know.

Yours very truly,
DUNCAN C. SCOTT, Deputy Supt. General.

WM. KEARNS, Assistant Auditor General, Ottawa.

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, March 27, 1923.

SIR, - I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter of the 9th instant (No. 116823 - 1), in reply to mine of the 27th
ultimo, with reference to the funds in the hands of Mr. W.M. Graham, Indian Commissioner, resulting from the sales
at the closing of the Elkhorn Industrial School. In that letter you state that the intention was to use these funds for the
purchase of necessary equipment at the reopening of the Elkhorn school, by doing which the appropriation for Indian
education would be supplemented.

This proposed method of supplementing your vote is entirely at variance with the principle of parliamentary control
over expenditure and with the provisions of the Consolidated Revenue and Audit Act. Section 2 of that Act defines the
term "public moneys"; Section 35 of the same Act directs that all public moneys, from whatever source of revenue
derived, shall be paid to the credit of the Receiver General; Section 41 directs that the Auditor General shall see that no
cheque issues for the payment of any public money for which there is no direct parliamentary appropriation.

These provisions of the Act form, in my opinion, an unsurmountable difficulty against the use or the proposed use of
the funds in question, which should be deposited forthwith to the credit of the Receiver General as Casual Revenue.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.
